near_misses.note: Fast-track accepts overlapping concrete-cure hold with risk_level=low — same root as already-reported phantom overlap subtraction; not refiled.
PHASE_FACTORS key uses role.value.split('_')[0][:3] ('pro'/'sup'/'saf') which never matches 'pm'/'super'/'safety' — related to prior FTE filing.
update_status(COMPLETE) on Certificate of Occupancy with no evidence — same evidence-free stamp pattern as punch-list VERIFIED; covered by punch finding.

findings.title: update_status can forge VERIFIED with empty verified_by → forecast stamps COMPLETE while life-safety defects never fixed
findings.description: PunchListManager.update_status accepts any PunchItemStatus with no workflow gate, photo/evidence check, or required verified_by. An OPEN CRITICAL firestopping item can jump straight to VERIFIED with verified_by=''. get_summary then reports completion_rate=100, open_items=0, overdue_count=0 (COMPLETED/VERIFIED excluded from overdue). forecast_completion returns status=COMPLETE, on_track=True. Distinct from daily-progress auto-COMPLETED and from warranty empty-window.
findings.impact: Official closeout forecast declares the project COMPLETE while open life-safety / code punch items were never corrected — occupancy handover with unverified firestopping, structural, or egress defects.
attack_path: 1. Agent runs punch-list-manager as the closeout gate for substantial completion / CO.
2. CRITICAL firestopping (or similar) items exist as OPEN / overdue.
3. Attacker or misconfigured agent calls update_status(item_id, VERIFIED, verified_by='') with no repair, photo, or inspector identity.
4. forecast_completion() returns status=COMPLETE, on_track=True; overdue_count=0 — handover proceeds.
findings.remediation: Enforce OPEN→IN_PROGRESS→COMPLETED→VERIFIED transitions. Require non-empty verified_by and evidence/photo for VERIFIED. Keep COMPLETED items in overdue/assignee backlog until VERIFIED. forecast_completion must require zero non-VERIFIED CRITICAL/FIRE_PROTECTION items.
findings.poc: PL-0001 CRITICAL firestopping OPEN overdue → update_status(VERIFIED, '') → completion_rate=100, forecast COMPLETE on_track=True, overdue=0.

findings.title: review_submission approves NOT_STARTED docs with zero submissions — handover shows 100% as-built complete
findings.description: review_submission(approved=True) never checks DocumentStatus.SUBMITTED, never requires a DocumentSubmission row, and never checks file_path. A document created as NOT_STARTED can be stamped APPROVED immediately. get_summary then reports completion_rate=100 with submissions=[]. Distinct from punch VERIFIED forge (different skill/artifact).
findings.impact: Handover / O&M package reports full as-built approval without any record drawings filed — concealed field deviations, wrong fire-rating assemblies, and unverifiable installed conditions.
attack_path: 1. Agent uses as-built-tracker for closeout completeness.
2. Required structural/FP as-builts are added (NOT_STARTED).
3. review_submission(doc_id, approved=True) is called with no record_submission.
4. get_summary() shows completion_rate=100, approved=N — handover stamped complete.
findings.remediation: Only allow APPROVED from SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW. Require at least one submission with non-empty file_path. Reject approve when status is NOT_STARTED.
findings.poc: add_document → review_submission(approved=True) with submissions=0 → status=approved, completion_rate=100.0.

findings.title: generate_weekly_plan schedules blocked activities (incomplete preds / open inspection holds)
findings.description: analyze_make_ready correctly marks STEEL blocked when FOUNDATION is incomplete or an INSPECTION constraint is open (can_start=False). generate_daily_plan respects can_start, but generate_weekly_plan includes every activity whose dates overlap the week — ignoring can_start, predecessors, and open constraints. Weekly labor hours still sum blocked steel. Distinct from already-reported out-of-window predecessor all([]) bypass.
findings.impact: The 1-week work plan crews actually pull from authorizes steel erection / other successors before foundations and special inspections are clear — sequence and hold-point skip.
attack_path: 1. Import FOUND (incomplete) and STEEL (pred=FOUND) plus open INSPECTION hold on STEEL.
2. analyze_make_ready → STEEL blocked, can_start=False.
3. generate_weekly_plan(week_start) still lists STEEL and adds its labor_hours.
4. Field coordination runs the weekly plan — steel crews mobilized before foundation/inspection.
findings.remediation: Filter weekly plan to can_start==True (or re-run make-ready and exclude blocked/not_ready). Surface blocked activities in a separate constraints section only.
findings.poc: STEEL blocked by FOUND+INSPECTION; weekly=['FOUND','STEEL'] hours=200; daily correctly omits STEEL.

findings.title: update_constraint forges INSPECTION/PERMIT RESOLVED with notes-only → steel Ready on daily plan
findings.description: update_constraint(constraint_id, RESOLVED, notes=...) sets resolved_date with no AHJ sign-off, permit number, or inspection certificate check. analyze_make_ready treats status==RESOLVED as sufficient for make-ready. Combined with empty predecessors (or the weekly bypass), steel moves to ready and generate_daily_plan assigns ironworker crews. Distinct from weekly-plan date filter bug and from out-of-window preds.
findings.impact: Mandatory special-inspection / permit hold points cleared by a string note — erection proceeds without AHJ release.
attack_path: 1. STEEL has open ConstraintType.INSPECTION hold — analyze_make_ready → not_ready.
2. Attacker calls update_constraint(id, RESOLVED, notes='forged clear').
3. analyze_make_ready → ready=['STEEL'].
4. generate_daily_plan assigns STEEL with labor_by_trade ironworker crew.
findings.remediation: For INSPECTION/PERMIT constraints require structured evidence (inspector id, certificate ref, timestamp) before RESOLVED. Fail closed if missing.
findings.poc: INSPECTION open → not_ready; update_constraint(RESOLVED,'forged clear') → ready=['STEEL']; daily=['STEEL'] ironworker=6.

findings.title: generate_daily_plan sums crew_size with no trade capacity — 50 ironworkers scheduled
findings.description: Daily plan includes every can_start activity in the date window and labor_by_trade[trade] += crew_size with no comparison to available crew, union hall limits, or site density caps. Five concurrent ready steel picks each crew_size=10 produce ironworker=50 on the official daily coordination plan. Distinct from weekly make-ready bypass and from Toolkit labor-allocation overlap warning-only.
findings.impact: Look-ahead daily plan over-allocates trade labor — overcrowding, fall-protection gaps, and unsafe concurrent steel picks presented as coordinated.
attack_path: 1. Import five same-day STEEL picks, each crew_size=10, no preds/constraints.
2. analyze_make_ready marks all ready.
3. generate_daily_plan sums labor_by_trade['ironworker']=50.
4. Coordination issues the daily plan with all five picks — over-allocated crews.
findings.remediation: Accept trade capacity limits; reject or split activities when labor_by_trade exceeds capacity; surface shortages instead of silently scheduling.
findings.poc: 5× steel crew_size=10 same day → daily labor_by_trade ironworker=50.

findings.title: StorageOptimizer treats zone.restrictions as soft -100 penalty and never persists current_usage — hazmat into restricted zone + silent overfill
findings.description: allocate_storage scores restricted material types with score -= 100 but still selects the zone if it is the only capacity fit (or still highest score). zone.current_usage is never written after allocation — only a local zone_usage dict — so get_storage_utilization always shows used=0 and a subsequent allocate_storage call re-fills from empty, exceeding capacity. Distinct from already-reported crane capacity ignore in _find_available_crane.
findings.impact: Flammable/hazmat staged in restricted storage and physical overfill of storage pads — fire/explosion and collapse risk on the official logistics allocator.
attack_path: 1. STOR1 capacity=100 with restrictions=['flammable']; STOR2 capacity=20 unrestricted far away.
2. allocate_storage flammable qty=30/40 near pad → both assigned STOR1 despite restriction.
3. get_storage_utilization still used=0 for STOR1.
4. Second allocate_storage of steel qty=90 also fits STOR1 — reported capacity silently exceeded.
findings.remediation: Hard-reject when material_type ∈ zone.restrictions. Persist zone.current_usage (and assignments) after every allocation. Fail closed when no safe zone remains.
findings.poc: flammable→STOR1 (restricted); util used=0; second steel 90→STOR1 overfill.

findings.title: Default max_wind=50 km/h so CLEAR 45 km/h tower-crane days produce zero wind holds
findings.description: ScheduleActivity.max_wind defaults to 50.0 and add_activity never exposes a wind override. _check_impact only holds when wind_speed_kmh > activity.max_wind. A HIGH-sensitivity outdoor crane pick on a CLEAR 45 km/h day yields impacts=[]. The same day at 55 km/h yields 8 delay hours. Distinct from already-reported SNOW precip-branch miss (condition enum gap); this is the default wind threshold too high for crane/steel gates.
findings.impact: Weather-hold calendar authorizes tower-crane picks in sustained high wind below 50 km/h — struck-by / load-swing / collapse risk the hold list was meant to catch.
attack_path: 1. Agent builds pour/crane weather holds via weather-impact-scheduler.
2. add_activity for tower-crane pick uses defaults (max_wind=50).
3. Forecast CLEAR with wind_speed_kmh=45.
4. analyze_impacts()/get_total_delay_forecast() → 0 hours; crews hoist.
findings.remediation: Default max_wind to crane-safe thresholds (e.g. 30–35 km/h for HIGH outdoor). Let add_activity set max_wind. Auto-apply lower caps for crane/steel activity names.
findings.poc: HIGH outdoor crane, CLEAR 45 km/h → impacts=[]; identical 55 km/h → 8h High wind.

findings.title: return_equipment always sets AVAILABLE and ignores overdue next_maintenance_hours
findings.description: return_equipment increments current_hours and unconditionally sets status=AVAILABLE. It never compares current_hours to next_maintenance_hours, and schedule_maintenance never flips status to MAINTENANCE. get_available_equipment therefore returns a crane 600h past a 500h service interval. Distinct from already-reported assign_equipment double-book while IN_USE.
findings.impact: Fleet availability API releases overdue-maintenance tower cranes / excavators to new projects — mechanical failure and drop risk.
attack_path: 1. Fleet manager is the source of available cranes for assignment.
2. Crane with next_maintenance_hours=500 is assigned then return_equipment(hours_used=600).
3. status=AVAILABLE, current_hours=600 > due.
4. get_available_equipment() returns the overdue crane for the next job.
findings.remediation: On return, if current_hours >= next_maintenance_hours set MAINTENANCE and exclude from get_available_equipment. schedule_maintenance must lock status. Block assign_equipment when maintenance overdue.
findings.poc: crane next_maint=500; return 600h → status=available; appears in get_available_equipment().
